# AEGIS — See what your AI agents are doing

> Your agents have access. You deserve visibility. AEGIS is an open-source local security dashboard for AI coding agents: detected process activity, file/TCP observations, project and skill reviews, Claude Code usage and audit reports. Windows first; macOS/Linux experimental. Monitoring does not automatically block commands.

## Purpose and scope

AI agents can access local files, credentials, shell commands and external services. AEGIS observes supported activity from outside the agent and records attribution evidence. It is one of several approaches to agent observability; in-agent instrumentation and OS-level tools have different coverage.

Monitoring runs locally without telemetry or an account. Optional AI analysis sends activity metadata to Anthropic using the user's API key; update checks contact GitHub. AEGIS has manual process controls but no automatic OS-level enforcement.

This document describes source capabilities and their limits. As checked on 13 November 2026 (UTC+04:00), the published Windows beta is [0.25.0-beta](https://github.com/antropos17/Aegis/releases/tag/aegis-v0.25.0-beta), released on 12 November (UTC) from d72101a5c48d246a500f23ee93d5431ce1772fe1. Release PR CI, master CI and the signed Windows build passed. Its downloaded installer passed Ed25519 signature, size and SHA-256 verification. Source CI and release publication do not establish fresh installed-runtime acceptance; [dated readiness records](docs/BETA-READINESS.md) retain their own tested package identities.

## 0.25.0-beta release context

The interface offers English, Brazilian Portuguese, Spanish, French, German, Japanese, Simplified Chinese and Russian. The six new catalogs are machine-translated with targeted corrections and still benefit from native-language review. Missing messages fall back to English. Anomaly toasts now use the translation catalog, and captured-result timestamps use the selected locale. Runtime and development dependency updates are listed in the [release notes](https://github.com/antropos17/Aegis/releases/tag/aegis-v0.25.0-beta).

JSON and CSV activity exports stage, flush and close a sibling temporary file before replacing the chosen destination. A failed attempt preserves the earlier destination; unconfirmed temporary-file cleanup is reported. The session-report IPC path rechecks its requesting renderer after generation before returning the result.

Claude Code token accounting keeps measured counts separate from local pricing uncertainty. Listed models with unverified rates, unknown-model fallback and uncertain cache categories keep pricing estimates explicit. Captured Local security, imported-result and container timestamps follow the selected interface language.

Local security documents comparison of imported before/after snapshots and untrusted claims, with search, change filters and retained-comparison refresh/clear. Incomplete snapshots leave changes unknown. Launch and project export stay unavailable from that comparison. The installed Windows package also supplies an explicit native owner-console route for one selected-file deletion, with mandatory terminal review and separate setup. See [returned-result comparison](docs/LOCAL-SECURITY-UI.md#compare-a-returned-result), [token accounting](docs/TOKEN-ACCOUNTING.md) and [selected-file deletion](docs/ACTION-DELETE-FILE.md).

Historical source checkpoint: 18 October 2026, merged master 96b63b165ac932e9615815f93c587765e6bde1b8 (PR #975). Packaged monitoring and file/TCP fixtures have source-bound results. Current Windows x64 source packages include experimental Kernel-File reads in Events, with an explicit local folder, Start and manual UAC consent. Capture stays off on startup; Stop, monitoring pause, suspend or quit request cleanup. Candidate paths and potential path-rule risk do not inspect contents or update risk scores, audit, baselines or sequences. Historical qualification includes the #975 warmup read, #976 diagnostic first/persistent reads and ordinary idle first reads after 65, 70 and 85 seconds on source 5249c10a. These receipts do not qualify changed protocol-10/package/harness inputs or a Windows restart; restart recovery remains unqualified. See [ordinary file reads](docs/development/ordinary-file-reads.md), [the agent-read guide](docs/development/agent-sensitive-read.md) and [Windows recovery admission](docs/roadmap/windows-recovery-admission.md).

## Installation

```bash
git clone https://github.com/antropos17/Aegis.git
cd Aegis
npm ci
npm start
```

Building from source requires Node.js 24.x, as declared in package.json and pinned in .nvmrc and CI. The packaged app ships its own runtime. Windows 10/11 is the primary platform; macOS/Linux remain experimental. For a browser demo, follow the built-preview instructions in the README.

## Features

### Process Monitoring

Tracks 112 known AI agents (265 process-name signatures across their `names` arrays) with parent-child tree resolution and IDE host detection. Covers coding assistants (Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor), autonomous agents (OpenClaw, AutoGPT, CrewAI, Devin), desktop AI (Gemini, Apple Intelligence), frameworks (LangChain, AutoGen, MetaGPT), and local LLMs (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp).

### File System Access

Watches sensitive directories (.ssh, .aws, .gnupg, .env, cloud configs) and the 35 AI agent config paths registered in AGENT_CONFIG_PATHS for file activity. Database configPaths metadata does not register watch roots automatically.

### Network Activity

Logs eligible observed TCP endpoints per detected agent PID with forward-confirmed reverse DNS and allowlisted, unknown or flagged verdicts. Provider outages and polling gaps limit coverage; an unresolved endpoint is not assumed safe.

### Behavioral Analysis

Applies 73 detection rules across 8 categories (AI config, secrets, SSH, cloud, browser, devtools, crypto, certificates) with rolling 10-session baselines and 4-axis anomaly scoring (Network/FS/Process/Baseline).

### Trust Scoring

Assigns real-time risk scores with trust grades (A+ through F) using time-decay algorithms and multi-dimensional threat assessment.

### Dashboard

Radar overview, summary cards, filtered/grouped activity feeds, network panel, expandable agent/application cards and footer sensor health. Monitoring presets: Paranoid, Strict, Balanced, Developer. Presets do not enforce OS-level blocking.

### Export and Audit

JSON, CSV, HTML reports, one-click ZIP archive and hash-chained JSONL audit logging with daily rotation and 30-day retention. Settings JSON and diagnostic ZIP exports omit the configured API key. Paths, endpoints and agent metadata in exports remain sensitive.

### YAML Rulesets

73 sensitive-path detection rules, validated against rules/_schema.json. Existing ruleset edits hot-reload in unpacked runs; packaged ASAR watchers are disabled. Extend by adding a .yaml to rules/ and reloading or restarting; sensitive-rule IDs must be unique and duplicates are skipped. Sequence correlations live separately in rules/sequences/: keep their IDs unique across files because the sequence loader currently does not reject cross-file duplicates.

## Technical Details

- **Stack**: Electron, Svelte 5, Vite; CommonJS JavaScript in main, TypeScript in the renderer and shared types. Exact versions: package.json
- **Tests**: Vitest; run `npm test` for current pass/skip and file counts
- **License**: MIT
- **Version**: 0.25.0-beta <!-- x-release-please-version -->
- **Platform**: Windows primary; macOS/Linux experimental
